$comment: D-CSUBSET-INT128-ICE-CONTEXT-REFUSED, the INVARIANT half of `examples/c/c_int128_ice_slots`. A 128-bit constant whose value does NOT fit an int64 must still FAIL LOUD in a 64-bit integer-constant-expression slot — it must never silently contribute its low 64 bits. ★★ THE BOUND IS A TRUNCATION TRAP, NOT A ROUND NUMBER: `((__int128)1 << 100) + 3` has low 64 bits of EXACTLY 3, so the two candidate behaviours are DISTINGUISHABLE — refuse, or a silent `int a[3]`. A `1 << 100` bound would have low 64 bits of zero and could not tell a correct refusal apart from a truncation to a zero-length array, which is the vacuity this file is shaped to avoid. ✔MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` and clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23`, probed SEPARATELY, both refuse it (on OBJECT SIZE — a different reason from DSS's, the same direction, both loud). The diagnostic is raised by the semantic tier's array-length rule with a source span, hence `positioned:true`; the load-bearing pin is the CODE plus a rejected compile. RED-ON-DISABLE: narrow the wide value through `low64()` in `asInt64` (src/hir/const_eval_arith.hpp) instead of testing its magnitude, and this compiles clean as a 3-element array, so the runner no longer finds S_NonConstantArrayLength.
